Hi Samir — appreciated the detail, that helps a lot. High-level guidance up front:

- H100 (preferred when memory and peak throughput matter): best for long-context 70B models and large KV cache footprints. Higher unit cost but orders-of-magnitude fewer nodes for very large context workloads. Good fit if you want single-GPU-hosted 70B with 32k+ context and minimal sharding complexity.

- A100 (balanced classic choice): strong for mixed workloads where you can shard or use tensor-parallel approaches. Cheaper than H100 on a per-GPU list price today; good for mid-sized models and when you can accept some sharding overhead and slightly higher latency at 99th.

- L4 (cost-optimized inference): much lower cost for 2–8B models and embeddings; limited memory for big 70B models unless you run heavily quantized/offloaded setups. Great for embedding fleet and lower-latency small-model chat, but you'd still need H100/A100 for the 70B chat model if you keep full precision.

I'll loop in Dev and the infra folks to draft a starter mix and quick TCO scenarios. Attached a short initial estimate. Proposed next step: 30–45 minute call to align on SLOs and whether Nova wants to optimize for latency or cost-first.

—Vanessa

Folks — forwarding Samir's note and the load profile. They want a starter fleet and one recommended proposal to put in the commercial SOW. High level asks: 1) H100 vs A100 vs L4 tradeoffs for this mixed chat+embeddings workload, 2) three candidate starter mixes (conservative/perf-first, balanced, cost-first), 3) callouts for gating items (perf tests, quantization feasibility, KV cache sizing).

My initial thinking (very rough):
- Conservative / perf-first: 8x H100 (primary for 70B chat), 12x L4 for embedding throughput and cost-effective burst capacity. This minimizes cross-GPU transfers and keeps chat latency tight.
- Balanced starter: 4x H100 + 8x A100 + 18x L4. H100s host the large-context chat instances, A100s for mid-size model inference and can absorb some load if H100s are saturated, L4s for embeddings and low-cost chat fallbacks.
- Cost-optimized: 2x H100 + 10x A100 + 30x L4 — relies on sharding and more aggressive quantization for the 70B and accepts higher 99th latency under peak.

Key tradeoffs we should call out in the SOW:
- Memory: H100 > A100 > L4. If Nova wants single-GPU 70B at 32k context, H100-class hardware will be required.
- Latency: H100 yields better p99s for long-context workloads; A100 will have slightly worse tail latency when sharded. L4 is optimized for cost but not for very long contexts.
- Cost: L4 unit cost is materially lower; heavy L4 strategies can reduce TCO but need compensating design work (quantization, more aggressive batching).

Can Dev and Laura run a quick sensitivity calc (ops per token, effective memory headroom, expected tokens/sec per GPU) and we’ll pick numbers for the proposal. Marissa / Rishi — if balanced looks viable, we’ll surface pricing and the recommended committed capacity.

—Vanessa

Thanks — ran a quick back-of-envelope using Nova's profile. Caveats: exact numbers depend on model family, quantization, framework kernels, and sequence distribution. Highlights:

Assumptions used: 70B decoder at 16k average context (peaks to 32k), quantized to 4-bit for A100/L4 runs where feasible. Embedding model is 2.7B, runs well on L4.

Estimated effective throughput (tokens/sec sustained)
- H100 (70B single-GPU high-memory optimized): ~1,400–2,200 tokens/sec (depending on batching and attention kernels). Good p99 headroom for chat at 2k token avg.
- A100 (sharded 70B): ~600–1,100 tokens/sec (sharding overhead and interconnect latency).
- L4 (small models/quantized 70B offload): ~300–700 tokens/sec for small/quantized workloads; not recommended as primary host for full 70B at large context.

Memory and KV cache callouts:
- For long-context sessions, KV cache grows linearly with tokens; H100 headroom helps avoid remote KV spilling. If Nova expects many concurrent long-context sessions, plan KV cache capacity carefully — that directly impacts required GPU count.

Sizing examples (rounded):
- Balanced proposal (4 H100, 8 A100, 18 L4) — supports ~6–8 steady long-context chat sessions on H100s (with headroom for spikes) and ~200–300 embedding qps on the L4 pool (with batching). A100s handle midsize chat bursts and act as redundancy.
- Cost-optimized (2 H100, 10 A100, 30 L4) — cheaper reserve cost but requires careful sharding and will show higher 99th latency during sustained peaks.
- Perf-first (8 H100, 12 L4) — best p99 and simplest ops model, but reserve cost is highest.

Next steps: We should run a 48-hour pilot with representative load (attack by sequence-length distribution) and collect real p50/p95/p99 numbers. I can spin a pilot job if we get test creds and a small model snapshot from Nova.
